success_patterns: Bare-definition clues ('It can mean to emit vapor or to show irritation', 'It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line') were solved by finding dictionary-style passages ('Define X', 'X - definition of X') that repeat the clue's definition text. The answer was the headword from those passage titles, given bare and in base form ('fume', 'Homestretch').

Clues of the form 'in this book/play/film' plus a character or plot detail ('Miss Havisham dies...', 'Goneril in this play') were answered with the work's standard title. The agent did not answer with the character, author or scene. The title that every passage pairs with the named character was the answer.
A clue asking for the 'title held ... by A, B & C' was answered with the shared title noun ('Emperor'), not one of the named people. The archive line or the passages for every name supported it.
Clue words that frame the answer were stripped: 'Barber of' + 'this Spanish city' gave 'Seville', not 'Barber of Seville'.

When the top passage merely repeated the clue with no answer, the agent used the entity that recurs across the other passages with the clue's distinctive details ('grandfather' + 'adding machine' -> William S. Burroughs), and gave the full name as the passages print it.

patch.reasoning: Several successes came from bare-definition clues, a work-title slot named by a character or plot detail, or a title shared by a list of real names. The skill covers type-matching in general but has no explicit bullet for the definition-to-headword lookup, the character-to-work-title mapping, or 'title held by A, B & C'. Each is a short bullet placed in an existing section, so no new top-level structure is added and nothing is reordered. Rule 3 and the Rule 4 trimming rules are untouched.

edits.target: A dictionary synonym that fits only one half ('trial') is wrong. When passages are noisy, use your own knowledge of sports terms and idioms.
edits.content: - BARE-DEFINITION clues ('It can mean to emit vapor or to show irritation', "It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line") ask for the dictionary HEADWORD that the definition glosses. Look for dictionary-style passages ('Define X', 'X - definition of X', 'X | Merriam-Webster') whose text repeats the clue's wording. The word in those passage titles is the answer. Give it bare, in the base form that fits the definition (verb for 'to emit...', noun for 'the part of...'). A synonym that appears only inside the definitions is wrong.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content:
- 'Title / office / rank held by A, B & C' (people from different countries or eras) asks for the ONE shared title noun ('Emperor'), not any listed person and not a country. Use the title that the passages or an archive line pair with every name.
- 'In this book / play / film / opera' plus a character or plot detail ('Miss Havisham dies when her dress catches fire', 'Goneril in this play') asks for the WORK's standard title (Great Expectations, King Lear), not the character, the author or the scene. Choose the title that the passages repeat beside the named character and the plot detail.
